title: backoff-advice-token-and-unified-error-frame-for-tool-function-streams
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: Customers observed ambiguous 429/503 scenarios from the OpenAI-compatible bridge during tool/function streaming. Clients need machine-readable guidance to decide between immediate retries, exponential backoff, or moving to a degraded model. This PR introduces a compact, opaque backoff advice token (Retry-Advice-Token) and a unified, machine-friendly error frame for streamed tool/function failures. Goals: (1) provide deterministic retry guidance without exposing internal load heuristics, (2) unify error fields across HTTP and streaming frames, (3) maintain backward compatibility with existing Retry-After headers and OpenAI shim behavior.
Design summary:
- New header: Retry-Advice-Token (opaque string). Token encodes server-side lease for idempotency/retry window and a short advice TTL (server-signed). Clients that receive a 429/503 can include the token in the next request to opt-in to server-coordinated retry behavior.
- Error envelope: all error responses (HTTP and stream frames) include an error_code (string), user_message, and optional retry_advice_hint ("immediate", "backoff", "abort") and a numeric backoff_seconds when applicable. This is added to the streamed frame format as a single line frame with "type": "error" and a consistent schema to avoid ad-hoc parsing.
- Idempotency interplay: when tool/function calls are tied to idempotency keys, the server may attach a Retry-Advice-Token to allow replay without requiring the client to change keys. The token is short-lived and scoped to the idempotency key+route.
- OpenAI shim mapping: updates mapper to surface the new fields from internal errors into OpenAI-style JSON error.body and to preserve Retry-After for clients that only understand the legacy header.
Migration and compatibility:
- Clients not updated will still see legacy Retry-After and HTTP 429/503 with user-facing messages.
- New clients can take advantage of the header + structured frame for coordinated retries and improved backoff.
Security and privacy: tokens are server-signed and opaque; they do not reveal internal load or topology.
Implementation highlights:
- server/http/headers.go: new header parsing and validation.
- server/streaming/frame_writer.go: emit unified error frames on stream close and mid-stream failures.
- shims/openai/mapper.go: map internal error_code -> openai error fields, and attach Retry-After fallback when token is present.
- runtime/idempotency/lease_manager.go: short-lived leases for token validation and eviction.
- docs/api/retry-and-errors.md: detailed client guidance and examples.
Behavioural examples (text):
- HTTP 429 with token: Response includes Retry-Advice-Token: "radv_eyJ...", body contains {"error_code":"rate_limit_capacity","user_message":"Region capacity high","retry_advice_hint":"backoff","backoff_seconds":12}
- Streamed error frame: a single line JSON frame: {"type":"error","error_code":"tool_execution_failed","user_message":"upstream tool timed out","retry_advice_hint":"immediate"}
Testing: integration tests cover token roundtrip, lease expiration, and shim mapping. Load tests verify no measurable latency regression.
Checklist:
- [x] header parsing and validation
- [x] stream frame emission and consumers updated
- [x] OpenAI shim mapping
- [x] unit and integration tests
- [x] docs and SDK sample update
- [x] security review notes included
Backcompat notes: if both Retry-Advice-Token and Retry-After are present, clients should prefer structured token flow when supported. When absent, fall back to Retry-After seconds.
Relationship to other work: this complements ENG-1093 (stream framing refactor) and replaces ad-hoc backoff hints embedded in logs.

release_notes: Introduce Retry-Advice-Token header and unified error frame for streamed tool/function failures. Adds structured retry advice (immediate/backoff/abort) and a machine-friendly error_code field. Backward compatible with Retry-After. Clients may opt-in to coordinated retry flow for improved availability.
